one_liner: Self-tuning C BLAS with part of LAPACK that times its own kernels on the build machine; about 6-8x faster than Netlib reference BLAS.
what_it_does: ATLAS (Automatically Tuned Linear Algebra Software) produces a complete BLAS with C (CBLAS) and Fortran 77 interfaces, plus natively tuned LAPACK routines for the LU, QR and Cholesky factorizations, which it can merge with netlib's LAPACK to give a full LAPACK. It links in place of the reference libblas/liblapack: the benchmark simply LD_PRELOADed it under R. You build it from source with ATLAS's own configure and make, and the install-time timing search tunes the library to that machine. It always produces static libraries, and with --shared also libsatlas (serial) and libtatlas (threaded).
how_it_is_fast: Automated Empirical Optimization of Software (AEOS): at install time ATLAS times candidate GEMM kernels and searches blocking factor, register blocking, unrolling and compiler flags with a relaxed 1-D line search. Where 'architectural defaults' from earlier searches exist for the detected CPU and compiler, it uses those instead. Contributed hand-written SIMD kernels (SSE, AltiVec, 3DNow! and others) are kept when they win, Level 3 BLAS is built on the tuned GEMM, and the LAPACK subset uses recursive LU and Cholesky and a hybrid recursive-panel QR. The threaded library uses pthreads with processor affinity.
when_to_use: Replacing the unoptimised Netlib reference BLAS through the standard F77 or CBLAS ABI on a machine where you can run the tuned build yourself: the benchmark shows 6-8x on 2800x2800 SYRK-type work even with an untuned generic Debian build.
A new or unusual architecture with no vendor-tuned or hand-tuned BLAS: the FAQ says the fully automatic search is there to give 'an adequate library on a truely new architecture'.
You want a BSD-3-Clause BLAS with a row-major C LAPACK interface (clapack.h) for LU, Cholesky and QR solves.
Studying or reusing empirical autotuning: the search framework and the per-architecture defaults are the reusable part.
when_not_to_use: Mainstream x86-64 or AArch64 where OpenBLAS, BLIS or MKL are available. In the same suite, single-threaded Debian ATLAS 3.10.2 took 1.50 s for the cross-product test against 0.49 s for OpenBLAS 0.2.12 and 0.14 s for MKL (both multi-threaded) on a Xeon E3-1275 v5. Multi-threaded ATLAS 3.11.38 only ties OpenBLAS, BLIS and MKL, within about 10%, on the older i7-4790K and i5-3570 hosts.

Prebuilt distribution binaries. Debian's libatlas3-base is built without processor extensions and Debian recommends a local rebuild (README.Debian, search snippet only). The ATLAS errata adds that stable 3.10's block-factor and storage constraints 'can cut performance by around half' on modern machines compared with the developer release.

Builds you cannot babysit. Configure aborts if it detects CPU throttling, parallel make (-j) ruins the tuning, tuning can fail with 'unable to get timings in tolerance', and open issues report a 3.10.3 tuning segfault with glibc 2.27 (#44), a failed RISC-V build (#78) and Cortex-A53 build problems (#79).
Applications that need a runtime-adjustable thread count or use OpenMP: the maximum thread count is fixed at compile time, and the errata calls an OpenMP build of ATLAS 'a bad idea' for speed.
Anything that needs active maintenance: no commits since 2019-06-11, and release requests #77 and #89 have no maintainer reply.

integration.form: static lib (always built) plus optional shared libs libsatlas and libtatlas (--shared); built from source with ATLAS configure/make, or as distribution packages
integration.dependencies: none for the C BLAS; a Fortran 77 compiler (gfortran) for the F77 interface and for full LAPACK from netlib's LAPACK tarball (--with-netlib-lapack-tarfile); pthreads for the threaded library
integration.min_toolchain: ANSI/ISO C 1990 compiler (gcc by default; clang on OS X from 3.10.3 with --force-clang); gfortran optional
integration.platforms: x86 32/64-bit, ARM (NEON on 32-bit), IBM POWER, SPARC; Linux, OS X, AIX, SunOS, Windows through Cygwin or MinGW; RISC-V does not build (open issue #78)
integration.thread_safety: FAQ: 'completely safe to call any ATLAS routine from a threaded code'; there are no global variables. Link the serial interface if you do your own threading. The threaded library's maximum thread count is fixed at compile time.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: link-level drop-in for the full reference BLAS (F77 and CBLAS ABI) and, when built with netlib's LAPACK, for LAPACK; ATLAS alone provides only the LU, QR and Cholesky-related LAPACK routines

gotchas: Harness note: the 'cross-product' row times R's crossprod(a), which R evaluates with BLAS DSYRK (symcrossprod in R's array.c), not DGEMM. The 'linear regression' row is solve(crossprod(a), crossprod(a, b)) on a 2000x2000 Matrix-package dgeMatrix, a SYRK plus a symmetric solve, although the script's printed label says 3000x3000. Each figure is the mean elapsed time of 10 runs.

Harness note: 'ATLAS (st)' is the generic Debian 3.10.2 binary, so ATLAS's install-time tuning never ran on the test hosts and the number understates a locally tuned ATLAS. 'ATLAS (mt)' 3.11.38 was built after slave-cmds.sh inserted 'thrchk=0;' into config.c, which disables ATLAS's CPU-throttling abort, and 'case 0x5E:' into archinfo_x86.c, which forces Skylake detection into an existing case. Its tuning therefore ran under whatever frequency scaling the performance governor left, and it is compared against a 2014 OpenBLAS 0.2.12 package.

Errata performance traps: serial performance can fall off a cliff for N > 1500 when the install leaves CacheEdge unset, so tune CacheEdge. Small-problem speed suffers because glibc's mmap-backed malloc makes ATLAS's per-call GEMM workspace expensive; the errata suggests MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=-1 and MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0 and then re-tuning. Hyperthreads thrash the caches, so disable SMT or pass --force-tids.
Threaded builds pin threads with processor affinity and are tuned for the configured core count, so a generic threaded library must be built (-t X) for the smallest core count of any target machine.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Siblings such as BLASFEO (small matrices), FT-BLAS, the GEMMFIP BLIS fork and Eigen are measured against OpenBLAS or MKL, while ATLAS clearly beats only the Netlib reference. Pick ATLAS only when you need a self-tuning, BSD-licensed full BLAS on hardware those libraries do not target, or when an existing build already expects libsatlas/libtatlas.
verified_claims_summary: The independent andre-wojtowicz/blas-benchmarks suite ran R-benchmark-25 under Microsoft R Open 3.2.4 on Debian Jessie, swapping BLAS libraries with LD_PRELOAD and reporting the mean elapsed time of 10 runs. On a Xeon E3-1275 v5, Debian's single-threaded ATLAS 3.10.2 computed a 2800x2800 crossprod in 1.50 s against 11.41 s for the Debian Netlib reference BLAS/LAPACK (7.6x) and the 2000x2000 regression in 0.747 s against 5.466 s (7.3x); on a Xeon E5-1620 v4 the crossprod took 1.58 s against 9.45 s (6.0x). Compiler and flags are not stated because both are binary packages.
status_note: Abandoned: the last commit is 2019-06-11, the last stable release 3.10.3 (2016-07-28) and the last developer release 3.11.41 (2018-10-05), and 15 open issues, including build crashes, have no maintainer replies. It stays BSD-3-Clause, still ships in distributions, and is worth building only where no better-tuned BLAS exists.
